Case study - Product & physical design

Faireez × Flow

When the loudest brand in the room learns to disappear.

Services
Product UX · Physical · Launch
Client
Faireez
Year
2025
Place
Flow Brickell, Miami

Faireez launches inside residential buildings with a loud playbook - lobby pop-ups, iPad kiosks, a fuchsia brand built to be noticed. Then came Flow Brickell, Adam Neumann's post-WeWork co-living project, engineered around "quiet," where nothing is allowed in the lobby.

I redesigned the entire launch to do the opposite of everything we knew: instead of standing out, blend in. Flow said yes. We launched.

Background

in-building, on demand

Faireez is an in-building home-services platform. The standard launch: concentrated days in the lobby, plastic iPad kiosks, a brochure booklet, residents signing up on the spot. It works - New York, New Jersey, Tel Aviv. In December 2025 we signed Flow Brickell, Adam Neumann's new luxury project on the Miami River.

The friction

no lobby. no noise.

Flow Brickell is part of a ~$525M, ~1,900-unit plan, rents $2,800–$6,000 a month - a dense pool of exactly the residents Faireez is built for. Then came the catch.

Flow is built on quiet - that calm is the product. The rule was blunt: nothing in the lobby, none of our usual activations. The entire playbook that had worked in every other city was disqualified before we set up a single kiosk. No registration means no residents, and the launch dies before it starts.

The insight

blend in, don't shout

Don't stand out -
disappear.

Faireez is a brand that shouts: fuchsia, uniforms, cart, brochures - every asset built to be seen. At Flow, being seen is exactly what gets you rejected. So I inverted the logic and entered through their brand language, not ours. Powered by faireez - Flow on stage, us as the engine. A chameleon.

The solution

physical + product

Physical. A solid-wood iPad stand in Flow's visual language. I designed it; a carpenter in Israel (Cohen Carpentry) built eight units by hand, flown to Miami.

Product. A registration flow rebuilt in Flow's design system. The kiosk video swapped for an AI film shot like an apartment scene. The NFC sticker reskinned into Flow's language - Spark your day.

The only fuchsia left is the one button that matters: submit.

Registration flow in Flow's design system - fuchsia only on submit.

The result

The design wasn't the multiplier.
It was the price of admission.

This isn't a story about lifting a number. Our conversion held at its standard benchmark - the design didn't move the rate. What it moved was the door. Without the chameleon approach, Flow says no, there's no launch, and that benchmark never gets the chance to exist. And it bought us a category we used to write off: quiet buildings.
